newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 493.75/494.75/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 493.75/494.75/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed weaker at 494.50/495.50 per dollar Monday as heavy corporate and interbank currency demand was unattended by the Central Bank, traders said.
Traders said the strong currency demand, particularly on the interbank market, was fueled largely by excess liquidity on money markets.
"The large banks bought a lot of dollars. The excess liquidity is fueling dollar buying and the Central Bank cannot contain it," one trader said.

The bolivar has depreciated at an increased rate in recent weeks, but Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said earlier Monday that the currency would be broadly stable during the remainder of the year.
Matos pointed to the size of the Central Bank's reserves -- $16.343 billion to July 21 -- as guarantee that there would be no sharp currency fluctuations.
"Almost every time a government official says that there is exchange stability the Central Bank restricts dollars and the exchange rate rise," one trader said.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
